description: A generated constant name is CFG_ followed by exactly six uppercase ASCII letters, no digits or other underscores.
A private test method is _test followed by exactly four lowercase ASCII letters. Nothing else.
An enum wire name is E followed by exactly four ASCII digits. Leading zeros are allowed.
A generated JS field is $ followed by exactly eight lowercase hexadecimal characters.
A CSS-module export name is exactly eight lowercase ASCII letters followed by _class.
Form-validation ticket: A snake-case field has 2 to 4 lowercase ASCII words separated by single underscores. Each word has 2 to 8 letters; no digits or leading/trailing underscores.

A JavaScript-style parameter is 3 to 16 ASCII letters, digits, dollar signs or underscores. It starts with a letter or underscore, cannot contain dollar anywhere except as its final character, and cannot be exactly null or true.
A generated array accessor is item followed by an index 0 through 63 without leading zeros, then literal []. No spaces.
A kebab-case event name is exactly three lowercase ASCII segments of 2 to 6 letters, separated by hyphens. No digits, spaces or extra segments.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. A test function name starts test_, followed by 3 to 12 lowercase ASCII letters or digits, beginning with a letter. The suffix cannot be exactly skip or todo; no further underscores.

Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search source text for a lowercase ASCII symbol 4 through 8 letters immediately after export= and before semicolon. No syntax parsing outside that substring.
Find a numeric register 0 through 31 immediately between lowercase reg[ and ]. Use shortest ASCII decimal spelling and search anywhere.
A Pascal-style class name consists of 2 or 3 segments. Each segment begins with one uppercase ASCII letter and has 1 to 5 lowercase ASCII letters after it. No acronyms, digits or separators.
A simplified assignment is let, one space, a lowercase ASCII variable 3 to 8 letters, equals with one space on each side, and that same variable plus literal .length;. No other text or spaces.

Code review requirement: A quoted property access is obj[ followed by a matching pair of single or double ASCII quotes around 3 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters, then ]. Property names null and true are forbidden; no whitespace.

An international code-review label: the literal prefix tag_ followed by 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed.

A code-review capsule: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper CODE{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }CODE. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring return. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

An LF-only symbol receipt has symbol= and 3 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters on line one, then copy= with the identical symbol on line two. No final LF or extra whitespace. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - A generated constant is an uppercase ASCII word 3 to 8 letters, underscore, the exact same word in the same case, underscore and a digit 1 through 9. The repeated word cannot be NULL or TRUE. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.

A stub declaration is fn plus one space, a lowercase ASCII name 3 to 8 letters, parentheses containing another lowercase ASCII name 3 to 8 letters, then colon and the exact function name. Function and argument names must differ. No other spaces or punctuation.
A compact year label is lowercase yr followed by exactly four ASCII digits. This is a label format, not a year range check.
A stopwatch tick is exactly five ASCII digits followed by lowercase ms, without spaces.
A duration entry is one or more ASCII digits followed by exactly one of the lowercase units sec, min or hr. Leading zeros are allowed; no spaces or signs.
The archive stores a day key as D followed by exactly seven ASCII digits, with no interpretation as a calendar date.
A scheduled batch label is T followed by exactly six ASCII digits and uppercase Z. Only digit width is checked, not time ranges.
Form-validation ticket: The reminder field is wait= followed by an integer 5 through 45 and lowercase min, no sign, spaces or leading zeros.
Time-picker value: 24-hour HH:MM, hour 00 through 23 and minute 00 through 59, followed by one space and either UTC or GMT, uppercase. No seconds.
A month bucket uses a four-digit ASCII year, slash, month 01 through 12, slash, and literal all. No calendar validation beyond the month range.
A date fragment is day 01 through 31, hyphen, month 01 through 12 and suffix ? immediately after the month. Format only: accept impossible calendar combinations.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. A timezone offset is uppercase UTC followed by plus or minus, two-digit hours 00 through 13 and colon plus minutes 00 through 59, or hours 14 with minutes 00 only.
Search filter, not whole-input validation. Find a two-digit minute from 00 to 59 immediately after lowercase minute= and before a semicolon anywhere in the text.
Search for an hour code 01 through 12 immediately between the lowercase marker hour[ and the closing bracket ]. Other text is allowed anywhere outside it.
An elapsed time is a canonical integer 0 through 99 followed by colon and two-digit seconds 00 through 59. No sign, spaces or leading zeros in the first field.

A scheduler comparison is due: followed by two identical 24-hour times separated by slash. Each time is HH:MM with hours 00 through 23 and minutes 00 through 59; no spaces. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.

Code review requirement: A date token has a four-digit ASCII year, a separator chosen from slash or hyphen, month 01 through 12, the same separator, and day 01 through 31. Only ranges and format are checked, not calendar validity.

A locale-specific month label: 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed.

A raw timer note: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper TIME{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }TIME. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring tick. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

A two-line clock receipt uses LF only: time= and a 24-hour HH:MM time (hours 00 to 23, minutes 00 to 59), then copy= and that exact same time. No final LF or other characters. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - A three-slot schedule consists of three different padded hours 00 through 23, separated by commas. No spaces; no hour can occur twice. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.
A shift span is start HH:MM, hyphen, end HH:MM in 24-hour format with padded hour 00 to 23 and minute 00 to 59. Start and end must not be identical; do not compare chronological order.
A short commit display is commit: followed by exactly ten lowercase hexadecimal characters. No branch, spaces or newline.
A CI artifact label is ci- followed by exactly eight ASCII digits and .zip.
A review key is PR followed by exactly six ASCII digits; leading zeros are allowed.
A task runner alias is task: followed by exactly five lowercase ASCII letters, no digits or punctuation.
A registry digest display is sha256: followed by exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Format only; do not compute the hash.
Form-validation ticket: A CI worker label is worker- followed by an integer 1 through 32 in shortest decimal spelling.
A release workflow branch is deploy/ followed by 3 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters, hyphen and an integer 1 through 99 without leading zeros. No other slashes or spaces.
A compact test result is passed= followed by integer 0 through 99, then ;failed= followed by integer 0 through 9. Shortest decimal spelling; fixed field order, no spaces.
A tooling label is @scope/ followed by a lowercase ASCII package name 3 to 12 letters, optionally hyphen and lowercase dev or cli. No other punctuation or uppercase.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. A migration filename is a four-digit ASCII sequence not all zeros, underscore, 3 to 12 lowercase ASCII letters, and .sql. Leading zeros otherwise allowed.

Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search terminal text for a build number 1 through 64 in shortest ASCII decimal spelling immediately after build= and before semicolon. Surrounding output is unrestricted.
Find an eight-character lowercase hexadecimal commit immediately between lowercase commit[ and ]. This is a contains search.
A container reference is registry.test/ followed by a lowercase ASCII repository 3 to 8 letters, colon and a canonical tag integer 1 through 24. No scheme, digest, path nesting or spaces.

A CI digest confirmation is verify: followed by two identical eight-character lowercase hexadecimal digests separated by slash. Format only, no hashing or spaces. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.
Code review requirement: A cherry-pick record is pick followed by one space, six lowercase hexadecimal characters, then literal ' -> ' and the exact same six characters. The hash cannot be all zeros.

A localized pipeline label: the literal prefix job: followed by 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed.

A CI output capsule: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper CI{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }CI. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring passed. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

An LF-only CI receipt is branch= followed by 3 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters, then copy= and the same branch on line two. No final LF, additional punctuation or spaces. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - A commit subject is fix or feat, an opening parenthesis, a lowercase ASCII scope 3 to 8 letters, then ): followed by one space, then the exact same scope and one space plus done. The scope cannot be tmp or skip. No additional content. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.

A workflow dependency is job: followed by a lowercase ASCII name 3 to 8 letters, then > and a different name with the same rules, then > and the exact first name again. No whitespace; neither name may be skip.
A staff handle is @ followed by exactly six lowercase ASCII letters; no digits or punctuation.
A service mailbox has exactly four lowercase ASCII letters before the literal suffix +bot@ops.test. Nothing else.
An account number is acct_ followed by exactly eight ASCII digits. Leading zeros are accepted.
A recovery alias is r- followed by exactly eight lowercase hexadecimal characters.
The directory login is exactly five uppercase ASCII letters followed by literal @STAFF. No domain parsing is involved.
Form-validation ticket: A bot username is bot followed by a canonical integer 1 through 40, no padding, spaces or separators.
A project mailbox is 3 to 10 lowercase ASCII letters, optionally followed by plus and 1 to 3 ASCII digits, then @team.test. No other local-part characters, spaces or uppercase.

A social handle begins @ and contains 4 to 12 lowercase ASCII letters, digits or underscores after it. The handle must start with a letter and end with a letter or digit; adjacent underscores are forbidden.
A departmental account ID is dept- then a canonical integer 10 through 72 and literal @internal. No spaces or leading zeros.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. A login is 6 through 14 lowercase ASCII letters or digits and must contain both kinds. It may start with a digit; exact names guest1 and admin1 are reserved.
Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search a message for a lowercase eight-letter user name immediately after user= and before semicolon. Surrounding text is unrestricted.
Find an account slot 01 through 24 immediately between lowercase account[ and ]. Search anywhere; the two-digit spelling is mandatory.
A forum username has 3 to 16 lowercase ASCII letters or digits, starts with a letter, and may contain single hyphens internally, never adjacent or at the ends. Count hyphens toward the length.

An account confirmation is login: followed by two identical lowercase ASCII usernames of 3 to 8 letters, separated by slash. No spaces. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.
Code review requirement: A migration address is a lowercase ASCII username 3 to 8 letters at old.test, then an arrow ->, then the exact same username at new.test. No spaces or plus tags.

An international display name: 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed.

A support search should succeed if any entire LF-separated line is suspended: followed by a lowercase ASCII username of 3 to 8 letters. Other lines may be arbitrary; a carriage return is not stripped from a line.

An LF-only account receipt has handle= and @ plus four lowercase ASCII letters on the first line, then copy= and the exact same handle on the second. No final LF or spaces. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - A namespaced login is a lowercase ASCII team name of 3 to 8 letters, colon, a lowercase ASCII username of 3 to 8 letters. Team and username must differ, and neither may be the exact reserved name root. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.

A tagged mailbox is a lowercase ASCII username of 3 to 8 letters, plus, a lowercase ASCII tag of 2 to 6 letters, at team.test. The tag must occur as a substring of the username; no other characters or uppercase.
A fallback field is exactly four lowercase ASCII letters, except the exact word null. No spaces or other characters.
A badge is exactly six ASCII digits except all zeros. Leading zeros are otherwise permitted.
A directory label is exactly five lowercase ASCII letters and must not start with tmp. No other characters.
The token is exactly eight uppercase ASCII letters, with no letter I or O anywhere. Nothing else.
A suffix key is exactly six lowercase ASCII letters, except it must not end in log. No spaces or other characters.
Form-validation ticket: A lowercase ASCII login has 6 to 12 letters, may not be exactly admins or system, and may not contain the substring test anywhere. No digits or punctuation.
A code is exactly eight ASCII letters or digits, includes at least one of each, and neither starts nor ends with a digit. The substring bad is forbidden in any ASCII letter case.

A file label has 3 to 12 lowercase ASCII letters or digits, begins with a letter, and may contain internal single hyphens. It must not start with tmp- or end with -old. Count hyphens toward length; no adjacent or edge hyphens.
A booking slot is slot- plus a canonical integer 1 through 64, except 13 and 42 are reserved. No padding or spaces.
Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. An eight-character lowercase ASCII hexadecimal token must include at least one letter a through f, and cannot be all f characters. No separators.

Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search for a lowercase ASCII name 3 to 8 letters immediately between name= and semicolon, excluding the exact names tmp and null. Other text may be anything.

Search arbitrary text for the lowercase token allow when immediately preceded by colon but not by deny: (the five characters immediately before allow). It must be followed by semicolon. Other occurrences or surrounding text do not matter.
A whitespace-free task key is 4 to 16 lowercase ASCII letters, digits or underscores, must start with a letter, and must not contain __, end in underscore, or be exactly none.
A pair record is two different lowercase ASCII words 3 to 8 letters separated by slash. Neither word may be root or null. No spaces or other text.
Code review requirement: A six-digit ASCII control code starts nonzero, has no adjacent repeated digit, and must not contain the substring 123 anywhere. No checksum or other characters.

An international alias contains 4 through 12 Unicode letters, includes uppercase and lowercase letters, has no adjacent identical code points, and must not contain any ASCII digit or combining mark. No normalization, spaces or other characters.

A quarantined note: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper SAFE{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }SAFE. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring clean. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed. The body must not contain the lowercase substring virus.

An LF-only exclusion receipt has key= followed by 3 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters other than root or null, then copy= and the exact same word. No final LF or spaces. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - A namespaced selector has three lowercase ASCII words 3 through 8 letters joined by colons. All three must differ; none may be root. No spaces or other characters. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.

A custom multiline record is START, LF, then 1 to 3 lines of 3 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters, LF, and END. None of the interior lines may be exactly skip or stop, and no two interior lines may be identical. No final LF, CR or whitespace.

no_match:
START
one
two
three
four
END

description: A thumbnail filename is thumb- followed by eight lowercase hexadecimal digits and .avif. Basename only; no path.
A daily spool path is /spool/ followed by exactly six ASCII digits and .dat. No other components.
A source filename is exactly eight lowercase ASCII letters followed by .mjs. No path or extra extension.
An environment file is .env. followed by exactly four lowercase ASCII letters. No spaces or path.
A Windows scratch filename is T followed by five ASCII digits and .TMP, uppercase. No directory portion.
Form-validation ticket: A rotated log filename is service.log. followed by a canonical integer 1 through 32. No leading zeros or compression suffix.
An image filename has a basename of 1 to 12 lowercase ASCII letters or digits starting with a letter, followed by .png or .webp. No directory or other dots.

A relative module path has 1 to 4 directories of 1 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters followed by a filename of 1 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters and .js. Slash separators, no leading slash, dot components or spaces.
A backup file is a lowercase ASCII basename 3 to 8 letters, .bak., and a canonical integer 1 through 99. No path, spaces or other suffix.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. Accept a basename consisting of 1 to 16 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, followed by .json. The basename may not begin with hyphen and may not be exactly null or true.
Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search a report for a six-digit ASCII spool number immediately after lowercase spool= and before semicolon. Surrounding text is unrestricted.
Find a backup generation 1 through 48 in shortest ASCII decimal spelling immediately between lowercase backup[ and ]. Search anywhere.
A Windows test path is exactly C:\temp\ followed by a lowercase ASCII basename 1 to 8 letters and .txt. Backslashes only; no extra directories or spaces.

A filename comparison is same: then two identical basenames separated by slash. Each basename is 3 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters plus .csv. No spaces or path components. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.

Code review requirement: A mirrored directory path is / followed by a lowercase ASCII directory name 3 to 8 letters, slash, the exact same name and .txt. The directory name must not be tmp or cache. No final slash.

An international basename: 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed. Append the exact literal suffix .txt after the name; its characters do not count toward the cluster limit.

An imported file note: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper FILE{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }FILE. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring path. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

An LF-only file receipt is file= and a basename of 3 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters plus .txt, then copy= and the exact same basename on line two. No final LF, spaces or path. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - A relative path has exactly two lowercase ASCII directory names 3 to 8 letters and a file named item.txt. The directory names must differ, and neither may be tmp or cache. Use slash separators, no leading slash. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.
A file checksum label is a basename of 3 to 8 lowercase ASCII letters, colon, six lowercase hexadecimal digits, colon, the same basename, colon, the same digest. Format only; no digest is computed.
An export identifier is uppercase EX- followed by exactly eight uppercase hexadecimal characters; no spaces.
A queue handle is lowercase q_ followed by exactly six lowercase ASCII letters.
A warehouse code is WH followed by exactly five ASCII digits and suffix X.
The short digest field has exactly ten lowercase hexadecimal characters followed by literal .sha, lowercase.
A scratch token consists of exactly eight ASCII letters from A through H, all uppercase, prefixed with tmp:.
Form-validation ticket: A generated shard handle is shard- followed by an integer from 1 through 64, no padding, signs or spaces.
A batch code is two uppercase ASCII letters excluding I and O, hyphen, then four ASCII digits. Digits cannot all be zero.
The trace token is exactly twelve lowercase hexadecimal characters, with exactly one hyphen after the sixth character. Uppercase is not accepted.
A job ID is JOB/ followed by a canonical decimal integer 100 through 250, with no extra text.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. A normalized opaque token is 8 through 16 lowercase ASCII letters or digits, must start with a letter and must contain at least one digit. No punctuation.
Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search arbitrary text for exactly eight lowercase hexadecimal digits immediately after digest= and before semicolon; the marker is lowercase.
Find a shard code from 00 through 31, padded to two ASCII digits, immediately after lowercase shard[ and before ]. Surrounding text is unrestricted.
A base32 voucher is 12 uppercase ASCII letters or digits, using only A through Z and digits 2 through 7, and must contain at least one letter and at least one digit.

A duplicate-digest field starts same: then two identical six-character lowercase hexadecimal strings separated by colon. No spaces. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.
Code review requirement: A palindrome code contains exactly six uppercase ASCII letters: the last three reverse the first three. The first three must be distinct.

The human-facing identifier alias: the literal prefix alias: followed by 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed.

An opaque ID memo: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper ID{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }ID. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring key. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

A two-line identifier receipt uses LF only. First line is id= followed by four uppercase ASCII letters, second is copy= and the exact same letters. No final LF or spaces. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - A compound ID has an uppercase ASCII letter, hyphen, four ASCII digits, hyphen, and the same letter. The four-digit serial must not contain any digit twice consecutively anywhere. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.
A routing identifier is one of east or west, colon, a two-digit number 01 through 24, slash, and the same region name again. The number 24 is reserved for west only.
A compact log event is EVT followed by colon and exactly six ASCII digits. No whitespace or message.
The trace-only log record is TRACE plus one space and exactly eight lowercase hexadecimal characters.
A server boot marker is BOOT[ followed by four uppercase ASCII letters and ]. No other output.
A log shard key is log/ followed by exactly five ASCII digits and literal /ready.
A process marker is pid= followed by exactly seven ASCII digits, including possible leading zeros.
Form-validation ticket: A queue log line is depth= followed by a canonical integer from 0 through 63. No signs, spaces or other fields.
An HTTP log summary is HTTP plus one space, status 400 through 499, one space and exactly GET or POST, uppercase. No path or other fields.
A timestamped event is HH:MM:SS then one space and either WARN or ERROR. Padded 24-hour time: hour 00 to 23, minutes and seconds 00 to 59. No other fields.
A worker line is worker= plus a canonical integer 1 to 32, one space and state= followed by idle or busy, lowercase. Exact field order, no other text.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. An access log message is path= followed by slash and 1 to 12 lowercase ASCII letters, one space and bytes= followed by a canonical integer 0 to 999. No additional path components or fields.

Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search raw server output for a request number 1 through 64 immediately between lowercase req= and semicolon. Shortest ASCII decimal spelling; other output is unrestricted.
Find an eight-character uppercase hexadecimal fault code immediately between lowercase fault[ and ]. Search anywhere in output.

Search LF-separated output for an entire line ERROR followed by colon, one space and 1 to 20 lowercase ASCII letters or spaces. At least one letter is required. Other lines may be arbitrary; CR is not a line delimiter.

A correlation summary is corr: and two identical eight-character lowercase hexadecimal IDs separated by slash. Nothing else is allowed. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.

Code review requirement: A paired operation log is OPEN followed by one space and a lowercase ASCII operation name 3 to 8 letters, one LF, then CLOSE plus one space and the exact same name. No final LF, CR, messages or other lines.

A localized log source: the literal prefix src= followed by 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed. Append the exact literal suffix ;ok after the name; its characters do not count toward the cluster limit.

A diagnostic block: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper LOG{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }LOG. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring error. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

An LF-only log receipt has trace= followed by eight lowercase hexadecimal characters on line one, then copy= and the exact same trace on line two. No final LF or spaces. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - An allocation log is take= and a canonical integer 1 through 99, semicolon, release= and the exact same integer, semicolon, free= and an integer 0 through 99 that differs from the taken value. No spaces or other fields. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.

A log transport marker is BEGIN, one ASCII space, a matching pair of single or double ASCII quotes around a lowercase ASCII label 3 to 8 letters, LF, then END plus one space and the same quote-label-quote spelling. The label cannot be tmp. No final LF.
A millimetre reading is exactly four ASCII digits followed immediately by lowercase mm. No sign, decimal or spaces.
A mass label is M= followed by exactly five ASCII digits and lowercase g. Leading zeros are permitted.
A sensor serial reading is exactly six lowercase hexadecimal characters followed by /raw, format only.
A display dimension token is W followed by exactly four ASCII digits and lowercase px.
A pressure export field is P: followed by exactly three ASCII digits and literal .0kPa. No spaces.
Form-validation ticket: A tilt setting is a canonical integer from 0 through 85 followed immediately by the degree symbol. No sign, decimals or spaces.
A battery reading is a canonical integer 0 through 100 immediately followed by %. No decimals, signs, leading zeros or whitespace.
A thermistor reading is an optional minus and a canonical integer magnitude 0 through 40, followed by °C. Negative zero is forbidden, plus signs and spaces are forbidden.
A lab volume is a canonical nonnegative integer with exactly one fractional ASCII digit, one space and either mL or L. No sign or grouping, case matters.
Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. A screen resolution is width x height with lowercase x and no spaces. Each dimension is an integer 100 through 999 in exactly three ASCII digits.

Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search telemetry for a humidity integer 0 through 100 in shortest ASCII decimal spelling immediately after humidity= and before percent. Other text is unrestricted.
Find a padded heading 00 through 35 immediately between lowercase heading[ and ]. Search anywhere, without interpreting physical angles.
A duration measurement is a canonical integer 1 through 99, optionally point and exactly two ASCII fractional digits, then one space and lowercase ms or s. No signs, padding or other units.

A measurement check is check: and two identical readings separated by slash. Each reading is a canonical integer 1 through 99 followed by mm, no spaces or decimals. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.
Code review requirement: A square label is side= and a canonical integer 1 through 99, lowercase x and the same integer, then one space and cm. No signs, leading zeros or decimals.

A localized unit name: the literal prefix unit: followed by 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed. Append the exact literal suffix :0000 after the name; its characters do not count toward the cluster limit.

A pagination label is page followed by one space and an integer from 1 through 64, in shortest ASCII decimal spelling.
A headline is 5 through 20 ASCII letters or spaces, begins and ends with a letter, and may not contain two adjacent spaces. No punctuation or digits.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. A list item is lowercase ASCII words 2 through 6 letters each, with 1 to 4 words separated by comma and one ASCII space. No terminal comma, other punctuation or leading/trailing spaces.
Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search prose for a lowercase ASCII label 3 to 8 letters immediately between label= and semicolon. Surrounding prose is unrestricted.
Search arbitrary text for the lowercase whole ASCII-letter word urgent. A boundary is start/end or any character other than an ASCII letter, so adjacent digits and underscores are acceptable.
A title has one uppercase ASCII initial followed by 2 to 11 lowercase ASCII letters, optionally one space and a second word with the same rule. No other characters.

An echo label starts echo: and contains two identical lowercase ASCII words of 3 to 8 letters separated by slash. No spaces. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.

Code review requirement: A quoted note consists of a matching pair of single or double ASCII quotes around 1 through 20 ASCII letters or spaces. At least one letter is required. No escapes, newlines or quotes inside the body.

An international single-word label: 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed.

A editorial note capsule: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper NOTE{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }NOTE. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring draft. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

An LF-only echo receipt is word= followed by a lowercase ASCII word 3 to 8 letters, then copy= and the exact same word on line two. No final LF or spaces. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - A three-word slogan consists of lowercase ASCII words 3 through 8 letters, separated by single spaces. The first and third words are identical and the middle word differs. No punctuation. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.

A text token has 6 through 16 lowercase ASCII letters, must contain exactly one of the substrings cat or dog, and that selected substring must occur exactly once. Substrings are counted by starting position, with no word-boundary requirement.
A French toggle record is one ASCII digit, colon, and exactly activé or désactivé, lowercase with precomposed accents. No whitespace or normalization.
A city key is 2 through 8 Unicode letters only. No spaces, digits, marks or punctuation; length counts code points.
A numeric glyph field is exactly four Unicode decimal digits, from any script; mixing scripts is allowed. No signs, spaces or other number categories.
A Greek label is exactly three code points, each both a Unicode letter and in the Greek script. Marks and punctuation are forbidden.
A Han tag is han: followed by exactly two Unicode letters in the Han script. No spaces, marks or punctuation.

Form-validation ticket: An international personal label contains 2 through 12 letter clusters. Each cluster is one Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. No spaces, initial marks, digits or punctuation; count clusters rather than code points.
A Latin locale label has 3 through 10 code points, each both a Unicode letter and in the Latin script. No marks, digits or whitespace.
An Arabic-digit reading is ar: followed by exactly four Arabic-Indic digits U+0660 through U+0669. Western, extended Arabic-Indic and other script digits are forbidden.

An international username is 4 through 12 Unicode code points, starts with a Unicode letter and then uses Unicode letters or ASCII digits. It must contain at least one ASCII digit; no combining marks or other digits.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. A Unicode heading is 4 through 16 code points consisting only of Unicode letters and ASCII spaces. It begins and ends with a letter and permits only single internal spaces; at least one space is required. Marks are forbidden.
Search filter, not whole-input validation. Find exactly four Han-script Unicode letters immediately between lowercase han[ and ]. Search anywhere; marks and punctuation do not count as letters.

Search text for the literal lowercase token café, precomposed, with no Unicode letter immediately before or after it. Digits, marks and punctuation are valid boundaries; case and normalization are not ignored.
An uppercase international code is 3 through 8 Unicode uppercase letters, followed by hyphen and two ASCII digits. Other letter categories, combining marks and lowercase are forbidden.

A bilingual code consists of 2 to 6 Latin-script Unicode letters, colon, 2 to 6 Greek-script Unicode letters. Marks, digits and spaces are forbidden. Each side must contain at least one uppercase and one lowercase letter within its own script.

Code review requirement: A Unicode echo token is 2 through 6 Unicode letters followed by slash and the exact same code-point sequence. Combining marks are forbidden, and the first half must contain both an uppercase and a lowercase Unicode letter.

An international identifier has 4 through 12 code points consisting only of Unicode letters, marks and ASCII digits. It starts with a letter, each letter may be followed by at most one mark, and every digit stands alone. It must include a mark and a digit; no adjacent digits.

A Unicode note: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper UNI{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }UNI. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring texte. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

An LF-only Unicode receipt has name= then 2 through 6 Unicode letters including both an uppercase and lowercase letter, then LF and copy= with exactly the same code points. No marks, spaces or final LF.

Acceptance criteria: - A Latin alias has 4 through 12 Latin-script Unicode letters only, includes at least one uppercase and one lowercase letter, and has no adjacent identical code points. Marks, digits and spaces are forbidden; no normalization is done. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.

A Cyrillic echo code is two distinct Cyrillic-script Unicode letters, colon, the same two letters in reverse order. Each code point must be a letter, not a mark; equality is case sensitive and no normalization is done.
A release serial is rel- followed by exactly six ASCII digits. Leading zeros are permitted.
A snapshot tag is snap. followed by exactly eight lowercase hexadecimal characters, no other components.
The channel revision is RC followed by exactly three ASCII digits, uppercase prefix.
A nightly build is nightly- followed by exactly eight ASCII digits and literal .dev. No calendar validation.
A preview tag is exactly four lowercase ASCII letters followed by -preview.
Form-validation ticket: The maintenance tag is patch- followed by a canonical integer 1 through 48, no leading zeros, signs or spaces.
A mobile version has literal v followed by three decimal components, each 0 to 99 with no leading zeros. Components use dots and no metadata or suffix is permitted.
A release branch is release/ and major 1 through 24, dot, minor 0 through 9. No padding or other components.
A package tag is a canonical integer 1 through 99, dot, canonical integer 0 through 99, optionally -beta. followed by an integer 1 through 9. No other suffix or metadata.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. An API level is api- followed by a two-digit level 01 through 32, optionally plus the literal suffix -legacy. No other suffix, spaces or lowercase changes.

Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search text for a revision integer from 10 through 79 immediately after lowercase revision= and before semicolon, shortest ASCII spelling; surrounding text is unrestricted.
Find an eight-character lowercase hexadecimal build digest immediately between lowercase build[ and ]. Search anywhere in the text.
A calendar-style release tag is r followed by four ASCII year digits, dot, and padded month 01 through 12. Optionally append -hotfix and a digit 1 through 9. Format only, no calendar facts.

A deployment confirmation starts deploy: and contains two identical tags separated by slash. Each tag is v plus major 1 to 99, dot, minor 0 to 9, both shortest decimal spellings. No suffix or spaces. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.

Code review requirement: A compatibility pair is a major integer 1 through 99, dot, a minor digit, slash, the exact same major, dot, a different minor digit. No leading zeros, padding, spaces or suffixes.

A localized release nickname: 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed.

A release note capsule: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper VER{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }VER. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring released. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

An LF-only version receipt has version= and v plus major 1 to 99, dot and a minor digit, then copy= and the exact same tag on line two. No final LF, spaces or suffixes. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - A build tag is b followed by a canonical integer 1 through 99, a separator chosen from dot or hyphen, three lowercase ASCII letters, that same separator and the exact same integer. The three-letter channel must not be dev. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.
A release range is v followed by a major integer 1 through 24 and .0, two dots, and v followed by the same major and . followed by minor 1 through 9. No padding or extra components.
An internal CDN route is /asset/ followed by exactly eight lowercase hexadecimal digits and .webp. No query, fragment or other text.
A CSS color field is the hash sign followed by exactly eight uppercase hexadecimal digits; shorthand and lowercase are not accepted.
The landing-page slug is /p/ followed by exactly six lowercase ASCII letters. No trailing slash.
An HTML data key starts data-x- and ends with exactly four lowercase ASCII letters. Nothing else.
A cache query is ?v= followed by exactly seven ASCII digits; leading zeros are allowed. No additional parameters.
Form-validation ticket: A local preview URL is exactly http://preview.local: followed by a port 8000 through 8099, then slash. Use four ASCII digits, no other URL components.
An image source is /img/ then 1 to 12 lowercase ASCII letters, then .png or .avif. No slash, query or whitespace in the basename.
Validate the fragment for a tab: #tab- then an integer 1 through 32 with no leading zeros. No spaces or other text.
An internal host consists of a lowercase ASCII label 1 to 10 letters long followed by .test, optionally followed by :443. No scheme, slash, hyphens or other ports.

Import gate — reject any nonconforming input. The upload accept field is a comma-separated list of 1 to 4 lowercase extensions chosen from .png, .jpg and .webp. No spaces; repeated extensions are allowed.
Search filter, not whole-input validation. Search arbitrary text for a lowercase six-letter route key immediately after route= and before ampersand. Other URL text is unrestricted.
Find a response status from 200 through 299 immediately between the lowercase marker status[ and ]. This is a contains search, not full input validation.
A download URL is exactly https://dl.test/ followed by a canonical integer 1 to 99 and either .zip or .tar.gz. No query, fragment, port or credentials.

A route-alias record starts /alias/ and contains two identical lowercase ASCII slugs of 3 to 8 letters separated by slash. No trailing slash or spaces. Each of the two values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes; the same quote character must be used for both values. Quotes are not part of the value, and escapes are not permitted.

Code review requirement: A simplified HTML tag pair is an opening tag with a lowercase ASCII name 1 through 8 letters, then 1 through 20 ASCII letters or spaces, then a closing tag with the exact same name. No attributes, nesting or newlines.

A front-end translation label: the literal prefix ui: followed by 2 through 12 Unicode letter clusters. Each cluster is a Unicode letter followed by zero to two Unicode combining marks. One optional ASCII hyphen may join two nonempty runs of clusters, but no edge hyphen or second hyphen is allowed. Length counts letter clusters, excluding the hyphen and any fixed prefix; spaces, digits and other characters are forbidden. No normalization is performed.

A captured web preview: the entire string has the literal opening wrapper WEB{, a lowercase ASCII routing label of 2 through 6 letters, colon, a body, colon, the exact same routing label and the literal closing wrapper }WEB. The body has 1 through 40 Unicode code points, allows any characters including line breaks and colons, and must contain the lowercase substring html. Only the body counts toward its length limit; no other text is allowed.

An LF-only route receipt has route= plus a lowercase ASCII slug of 3 to 8 letters on line one, and copy= plus the same slug on line two. No final LF or other content. Both values must be enclosed in matching ASCII single or double quotes, using the same quote character on both lines. The quotes are delimiters, not part of the value; no escapes are permitted.

Acceptance criteria: - Validate exactly /tenant/<name>/mirror/<name>, where both names are the same lowercase ASCII slug of 3 to 8 letters. The reserved names admin and root are forbidden; no other components or trailing slash. - Evaluate the input as supplied; do not trim or normalize it.
A two-parameter query is ?left= and a canonical integer 1 to 99, then &right= and another such integer. Values must differ; parameter order is fixed and no extra parameter is allowed.
